value_stream.name: Self-Checkout, Scan-&-Go & Unattended Retail Technology Operations

fields.Owner: Head of Frontend/Store Ops (VS-07/VS-08) / Strategy (VS-33) / IT (VS-27)
fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), POS (VS-08), Strategy (VS-33), IT/EA (VS-27/VS-113), Loss Prevention (VS-23), Finance (VS-17.4), HR (VS-19/VS-103)
fields.Trigger: Strategy review; wage/queue pressure; format evolution
fields.Volume: One enterprise SCO/scan-&-go/unattended strategy across 200 stores

workflows.name: Self-Checkout & Unattended Retail Strategy, Scope & Operating Model

Automation Opportunity: - Business-case modeler with loss-rate sensitivity; store-profile-segmented rollout planner; ROI tracker
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: strategy approved (COO/CIO/CFO); business case incl. loss-rate; format segmented by store profile; phased rollout
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-08 (POS), VS-27/VS-113 (IT/EA), VS-23 (LP), VS-17.4 (FP&A), W4434 (technology), W4437 (loss), W4440 (change)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Loss-rate-blindness risk**: SCO deployed without loss modeling → shrink blowout erodes wage savings; mitigated by upfront loss-rate modeling & LP design (W4437)
- **Format-mismatch risk**: wrong format per store profile (e.g. scan-&-go in low-digital-province store); mitigated by store-profile-segmented rollout
System Touchpoints: - Strategy (VS-33); POS (VS-08); store-ops (VS-07); IT/EA (VS-27/VS-113); LP (VS-23); finance FP&A (VS-17.4); capex (VS-40)

steps.activity: Strategy/Frontend set the SCO/scan-&-go strategy — objective (wage savings, queue reduction, trade-pro experience), format mix (banked SCO, mobile scan-&-go, locker/vending, unattended), phased rollout by store profile
Finance/LP model the business case — capex (VS-40), wage offset, expected SCO loss-rate vs staffed, ROI/payback, and the loss-prevention investment to keep SCO shrink acceptable
Strategy/Frontend document the strategy, obtain approval, and cascade to technology (W4434), layout (W4435), loss-prevention (W4437), change management (W4440)

fields.Participants: IT (VS-27), EA (VS-113), POS (VS-08), LP (VS-23), Security (VS-27.3), Vendor (VS-34), BI (VS-28)
fields.Volume: One SCO/scan-&-go technology stack across 200 stores

Automation Opportunity: - Reference architecture; integration patterns; pilot checklist; transactional-integrity test harness
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: technology security-assessed (VS-27.3); integrated real-time to POS/payment/loyalty/e-invoicing; offline-capable; pilot-validated
Cross-references: - links to VS-27 (IT), VS-113 (EA), VS-08 (POS), VS-80 (payment), VS-75 (app), W4433 (strategy), W4446 (uptime)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Integration-gap risk**: SCO not synced to real-time inventory/price/promo → wrong price/stockout mis-handling; mitigated by event-streaming integration
- **Offline-gap risk**: SCO fails on outage; mitigated by offline-capable design (POS-equivalent ≥8hr)
System Touchpoints: - SCO/scan-&-go platform; POS-ERP (VS-08); mobile app (VS-75); payment (VS-80); loyalty (VS-13); security (VS-27.3); BI (VS-28); vendor (VS-34)

steps.activity: IT/EA/Frontend select the SCO/scan-&-go technology — SCO terminals, scan-&-go mobile app (links VS-75), computer-vision/just-walk-out, cash-recycler, weight-scale, integration to POS-ERP (VS-08) inventory/price/promo real-time
IT/EA design the architecture — offline-capable (like POS ≥8hr), real-time sync (<30s), security (VS-27.3), integration to payment-gateway (VS-80), loyalty (VS-13), e-invoicing (BIR)
IT/Vendor deploy, pilot, and validate transactional integrity (price/promo/tax) vs staffed POS before scale

workflows.name: SCO Lane Layout, Store Design & Capacity Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Capacity-sizing model from transaction/peak data; layout templates with LP sight-lines; throughput-based right-sizing
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: capacity profile-sized; LP sight-lines in layout; BP 344 accessibility; throughput-validated (W4455)
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store), VS-20/VS-109 (RE/remodel), VS-55 (visual merch), VS-23 (LP), VS-147 (safety), W4454 (accessibility), W4455 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Capacity-mismatch risk**: too few SCO → queue; too many → idle capex; mitigated by profile-based sizing & throughput validation
- **Sight-line risk**: poor layout hides scan-avoidance from attendant; mitigated by LP-into-layout design
System Touchpoints: - Store-ops/design (VS-07/VS-20/VS-109); visual merch (VS-55); LP/CCTV (VS-23); IFM (VS-138); customer safety (VS-147); footfall (VS-28)

steps.activity: Frontend/Real Estate size SCO capacity per store profile (transaction volume, peak queue, basket size, trade-pro vs DIY mix) and design the lane layout (banked SCO pod, attendant station, sight-lines, intervention queue)
LP/Visual Merch design loss-prevention-into-layout (attendant sight-lines, exit-control, mirror/camera coverage) and accessibility (wheelchair reach, screen, PWD lane) per BP 344 (links VS-147/W4454)
Store Ops/IFM implement (fixture, power/data, signage), validate capacity in pilot, and adjust on throughput data (W4455)

fields.Participants: App (VS-75), Ecommerce (VS-10), Frontend (VS-08), IT (VS-27), LP (VS-23), Loyalty (VS-13), Privacy (VS-91)
fields.Volume: One scan-&-go program (mobile app + device-supplied handheld)

Automation Opportunity: - Risk-based exit-audit engine; scan-pattern anomaly detection; adoption analytics; privacy-by-design app data
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: scan-&-go flow integrated real-time; risk-based exit-verification; privacy-by-design (VS-91); adoption/loss measured (W4455)
Cross-references: - links to VS-75 (app), VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-08 (POS), VS-80 (payment), VS-13 (loyalty), VS-91 (privacy), W4437 (loss), W4450 (exception)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scan-avoidance risk**: customer skips items in scan-&-go → high shrink if no exit-verify; mitigated by risk-based exit audit
- **Adoption risk**: low BYOD adoption in low-digital-province stores; mitigated by device-supplied option & segmented rollout
System Touchpoints: - Mobile app (VS-75); ecommerce (VS-10); POS-ERP (VS-08); payment (VS-80); loyalty (VS-13); LP/exit-verify (VS-23); privacy (VS-91); BI (VS-28)

steps.activity: App/Frontend design the scan-&-go flow — BYOD (customer's phone via app) and/or device-supplied handheld, scan→bag→pay→verify-exit, loyalty/price/promo real-time, payment (VS-80) integration
LP design the **exit-verification** control (random/AI-risk-based audit, weight/visual match) to deter scan-avoidance without fricting all customers, and privacy-by-design for app data (VS-91)
App/IT pilot scan-&-go in profile-segmented stores, measure adoption/loss (W4455), and scale

fields.Participants: LP (VS-23), Frontend (VS-08), IT (VS-27), BI (VS-28), Security (VS-27.3), Vendor (VS-34)

Automation Opportunity: - Weight-cross-check engine; CV SKU-recognition; barcode-swap detection; exception-case auto-routing (W4450); threshold auto-tuning
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: weight-security + item-recognition; barcode-swap/sweethearting detection; intervention protocol trained; loss reviewed (W4455)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-115 (calibration), VS-23.2 (CCTV), W4434 (technology), W4449 (fraud), W4450 (exception), W4455 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Weight-spoofing risk**: customer manipulates scale or bags after scan → scan-avoidance; mitigated by item-recognition + intervention
- **Barcode-swap risk**: cheap barcode scanned on expensive item; mitigated by SKU-recognition CV + swap-detection
System Touchpoints: - SCO weight-scale (VS-115 calibration); computer-vision; LP/exception (VS-23/W4450); BI (VS-28); CCTV (VS-23.2); security (VS-27.3)

steps.activity: LP/IT specify the weight-security design — bagging-area scale cross-check (expected vs actual weight per item), item-recognition camera, and intervention-prompt on mismatch (the core SCO anti-scan-avoidance control)

LP/IT layer computer-vision/analytics — SKU-recognition (e.g. produce/bulk), barcode-swap detection (cheap barcode on expensive item), "sweethearting" (attendant override pattern), and exception-casework (W4450)
LP/Frontend tune thresholds (false-positive vs detection), train attendants on intervention protocol, and review loss data (W4455) to iterate

fields.Participants: Frontend (VS-08), Compliance (VS-22), DG (VS-114), LP (VS-23), HSE (VS-24), Store Ops (VS-07), IT (VS-27)
fields.Volume: Age-restricted (cutting tools, solvents) + DG/hazmat + catch-weight items in SCO

Automation Opportunity: - Item-flag rule-engine; attendant-intervention workflow; DG block-list; catch-weight auto-measure; adherence analytics
Controls: - CTL-677: age/hazmat/controlled item-flag; attendant intervention required; DG block-list; adherence audited
Cross-references: - links to VS-08 (POS), VS-114 (DG), VS-24.3 (hazmat), VS-22 (compliance), VS-115 (calibration), W4434 (technology), W4443 (intervention ops)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Age-verification-bypass risk**: minor buys age-restricted via SCO; mitigated by item-flag + attendant ID-check
- **DG-in-SCO risk**: hazmat sold via SCO without control; mitigated by DG block-list / attendant-required flag
System Touchpoints: - SCO/POS item-control (VS-08); DG (VS-114); HSE hazmat (VS-24.3); compliance (VS-22); calibration/catch-weight (VS-115); LP (VS-23)

steps.activity: Compliance/Frontend define the SCO item-control policy — age-restricted (cutting tools, solvents/aerosols — profile §5), DG/hazmat (paint/thinners/chemicals — links VS-114), controlled (catch-weight, cut-to-length), and the attendant-intervention requirement
IT/Frontend build the intervention flow — SCO flags age/hazmat/controlled item → attendant ID-verify (age), authorize, weigh/measure (catch-weight VS-115), or block (DG not SCO-eligible), per policy
Compliance/Store train attendants on intervention (ID-check, hazmat handling, DG block list), audit adherence (links VS-146), and tune the flag set

fields.Participants: Strategy (VS-33), Store Ops (VS-07), IT/EA (VS-27/VS-113), LP (VS-23), Real Estate (VS-97), Legal (VS-100), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Volume: Unattended formats (micro-stores, lockers, vending, contactless) — pilot

Automation Opportunity: - Remote-monitoring/access-control; emergency-comms; fire/life-safety automation; e-invoicing integration; incident-alert routing
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: access-controlled; CCTV/fire/life-safety; emergency comms; regulatory-permit confirmed; pilot-validated
Cross-references: - links to VS-75 (app), VS-80 (payment), VS-23 (LP/access), VS-138 (fire/life-safety), VS-147 (safety), VS-79 (BIR), W4433 (strategy)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unattended-safety risk**: no staff on-site → incident/assault/fire response gap; mitigated by remote monitoring, emergency comms, fire/life-safety
- **Regulatory risk**: 24-hr/unattended permit/e-invoicing non-compliance; mitigated by legal/compliance pre-check
System Touchpoints: - Access-control/app (VS-75); payment (VS-80); CCTV/access (VS-23); fire/life-safety (VS-138); BIR e-invoicing (VS-79); customer safety (VS-147)

steps.activity: Strategy/Store design the unattended format — 24-hr micro-store, click-&-collect locker (links VS-10 BOPIS), vending, contactless — with access (app/member), payment, and the use-case fit
LP/HSE design unattended-format safety & security — CCTV, access-control, fire/life-safety (BFP), emergency comms, no-staff incident response (links VS-147), and LP coverage
Legal/Compliance confirm regulatory fit (LGU permit for 24-hr/unattended, BIR CAS/e-invoicing, age-restricted sale rules) and pilot before scale

fields.Participants: HR (VS-103), OCM (VS-134), Store Ops (VS-07), Frontend (VS-08), L&D (VS-19.4), Labor Relations (VS-84)

workflows.name: SCO Acceptance, Change Management & Associate Role Redesign

Automation Opportunity: - Change-management playbook; role-redeployment planner; adoption/resistance analytics; redeployment-to-value tracking
Controls: - CTL-677 (ensure controlled execution — Self-Checkout & Scan-&-Go Strategy, Design & Technology (PA-149.1).)
- CTL-677: change-managed rollout; role-evolution communicated; labor-relations engaged; freed hours redeployed to value; adoption measured
Cross-references: - links to VS-134 (OCM), VS-103 (HR/EX), VS-19.4 (L&D), VS-84 (labor), VS-124 (enablement), W4455 (adoption analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Resistance risk**: associates/cashiers resist SCO (job-security fear); mitigated by role-evolution comms & redeployment
- **Labor-relations risk**: unilateral role change → grievance; mitigated by engagement (VS-84) & change management (VS-134)
System Touchpoints: - OCM (VS-134); HR/EX (VS-103); L&D (VS-19.4); labor relations (VS-84); store-ops (VS-07); enablement (VS-124); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: HR/OCM run change management — stakeholder engagement, associate comms (SCO is role-evolution not replacement), sponsor activation, resistance management (links VS-134)
HR/Frontend redesign the cashier→SCO-attendant role (monitoring, intervention, assistance, loss-prevention), retrain (VS-19.4), and manage any labor-relations engagement (VS-84)
Store Ops/HR redeploy freed labor-hours to value-add (assistance, replenishment, clienteling VS-124) rather than pure reduction, and measure adoption (W4455)
